summary: An interior news page of The Anaconda Standard dated Tuesday, 29 April 1890, dense with local Butte and Montana news across six columns. The page carries a mix of accident reporting, court proceedings, real estate notices, and local briefs, alongside substantial advertising columns on the right-hand side for Maguires Opera House, Northern Pacific Railroad land sales, and various Butte merchants. Editorial tone is brisk and factual, with several prominent multi-deck headlines signalling serious incidents — a mine fatality, a murder trial, and a court estate ruling — surrounded by shorter items under section heads for police, real estate, and miscellaneous city news.
headlines: IT WILL BE A BIG AFFAIR

clipping_placements.placement_note: top of col 1, under its own bold multi-deck headline; the first major story the eye reaches on the page

juxtapositions: The account of Patrick Murphy's death in the mine shaft — leaving seven children, the eldest a boy of 10 working at the same mine — sits directly alongside a column advertising 170 lots sold in the Northern Pacific Addition to Butte, projecting boom-town prosperity a column away from a family's ruin.
The 'IT WILL BE A BIG AFFAIR' report on a large new foundry planned for Butte runs just below the Murphy mine-death story, setting industrial ambition immediately beneath an industrial fatality.
